neighbours.label: Advanced analysis with special functions: gamma, zeta and Bessel functions, analytic continuation, divergent or asymptotic series (text or code)
fire: The functional equation relates the zeta function at s to its value at 1 - s through the gamma function.
Borel summation assigns a finite value to the divergent series by analytic continuation of its transform.
For large arguments the modified Bessel function behaves like an exponential divided by a square root, times an asymptotic series.

assert gamma(x + 1).rewrite(factorial) == factorial(x)
    assert expint(1, x).series(x, 0, 3) == -EulerGamma - log(x) + x - x**2/4
The incomplete gamma function has an analytic continuation to the whole complex plane, apart from a branch cut.
Stirling's formula gives the leading term of the asymptotic series for the logarithm of the gamma function.
The Dirichlet L-function is defined by a series for large real part and extended by analytic continuation.
The error function erf and the exponential integral Ei are both expressed through the confluent hypergeometric function.
quiet: The quadratic equation relates the roots of the polynomial to its coefficients through the discriminant.
The sample mean assigns an average value to the data set by dividing the total by the count.
For large samples the binomial distribution looks like a normal curve centred on the mean, with a small spread.

assert area(3, 4) == 12
    assert perimeter(3, 4) == 14
    assert round(average([1, 2, 6]), 2) == 3.0
The rotation matrix has an inverse equal to its transpose, apart from a change of sign.
Pythagoras's theorem gives the length of the hypotenuse from the lengths of the other two sides.
The median is defined as the middle value of a sorted list and found by counting.
The slope and the intercept of the line are both computed from the two given points.
